description:
## Problem

/lets:pr flow jumps between phases without user confirmation:
- After Phase 1 (review analysis) -> immediately transitions to Phase 2 (discuss findings) with no pause
- Line 262 in pr.md: "Transition to Phase 2 immediately (no need for separate invocation)"
- User has no chance to review the summary, read the JSON, or decide whether to proceed

## Expected Behavior

Every phase transition should have an AskUserQuestion gate with options to:
- Continue to next phase
- Skip phase (e.g., skip discussion, post all as-is)
- Save and exit (resume later with `/lets:pr`)
- Cancel review entirely

## Specific Gates to Add

1. **After Phase 1 summary (2.5)** - before entering Phase 2 discussion:
   - "Continue to discuss findings?" / "Post all without discussion" / "Save for later" / "Cancel"

2. **Review Phase 2 finding-by-finding flow** - already has AskUserQuestion per finding (good), but add:
   - Batch option: "Apply same disposition to remaining {N} findings" when pattern emerges
   
3. **Verify Phase 3 (follow-up) and Phase 4 (approve) also have gates** - audit all phase transitions

## Acceptance Criteria

- No phase transition happens without user confirmation
- Every gate has a "save for later" option (leverages existing state file)
- Every gate has a "skip"/"cancel" option
- Finding-by-finding discussion has batch shortcut for remaining items
title: Add user confirmation gates to /lets:pr flow

## Planner Agent

Create `lets:planner` agent - analog of built-in `Plan` subagent but with our rules and conventions.

Built-in `Plan` agent: read-only (Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput), returns architectural plans. No Edit/Write.

Our `lets:planner` should:
- Same read-only toolset as built-in Plan
- Follow lets conventions (project boundaries, stack idioms, existing patterns)
- Output structured implementation plan compatible with /lets:execute
- Be dispatched by /lets:plan command

/lets:plan command uses EnterPlanMode/ExitPlanMode for the main flow, dispatches lets:planner agents for codebase exploration and architecture design.

description:
Interactive worktree sessions - run multiple Claude Code instances on different tasks in parallel.

## Use Case
User opens 2+ terminals, each working on a separate task in its own worktree.
Each terminal has full LETS workflow: /lets:start, /lets:commit, /lets:done.

## Architecture (updated 2026-03-01)

Agent worktrees (isolation:worktree) use NATIVE Claude Code behavior:
- Created at .claude/worktrees/<name>/
- Auto-cleanup when agent finishes without changes
- No hooks, no .lets/ symlink, no .beads/redirect needed
- Agents only do code work, don't run LETS commands

Interactive worktrees need EXTRA setup:
- .lets/ symlink -> main .lets/ (for /lets:start, config, sessions, plans)
- .beads/redirect via bd worktree create (for bd commands to use shared database)
- Worktree branch used as-is (no feature branch creation)

## Implementation
- New command: commands/worktree.md
- Subcommands: create, list, remove, info
- create: git worktree add + bd worktree create + .lets/ symlink
- Location: .worktrees/ at project root (not .claude/worktrees/ - that's for agents)
- Verify .gitignore before creating
- Show LETS box with next steps

## Known Issues to Handle
1. /lets:start Step 6 creates feature branch in worktree - needs worktree detection to skip
2. .session-start-ref shared file - needs per-branch naming for parallel sessions
3. last-summary.md last-writer-wins - acceptable (dated archives exist)
4. .lets/ trailing slash in .gitignore doesn't match symlinks - fixed (.lets without slash added)

## Test Scenario
1. Terminal 1: normal session on task A
2. Terminal 2: /lets:worktree create (or claude --worktree with future hook)
3. Terminal 2: /lets:start -> pick task B -> work -> /lets:commit
4. Verify: shared beads, shared .lets/config.yaml, independent sessions

Reference: docs/knowledge/worktree-and-agent-teams-guide.md
title: Create /lets:worktree command - worktree lifecycle management

description:

gh pr diff works from any branch - no checkout needed. Agents only need the diff, not the actual files on disk.

Fix: detect worktree context in /lets:pr and skip branch checkout. Use gh pr diff exclusively.

description:
## Problem

bd dolt push and bd dolt pull always fail with 'invalid connection' when using git+https remote (e.g. GitHub).

The operations actually complete successfully on the dolt server side, but bd client disconnects before getting a response.

## Root Cause

In internal/storage/dolt/store.go:646, buildServerDSN sets:
```go
params := "parseTime=true&timeout=5s&readTimeout=10s&writeTimeout=10s"
```

readTimeout=10s and writeTimeout=10s are too short for remote operations. A dolt push to git+https://github.com remote takes 30-90 seconds (git fetch + upload). The MySQL connection times out at 10s, bd reports 'invalid connection', but the server completes the push successfully.

## Evidence

- `bd dolt push` -> `[mysql] packets.go:58 read tcp 127.0.0.1:XXXXX->127.0.0.1:13771: i/o timeout`
- Server log shows no errors, connection lives for 30-40 seconds
- Direct `cd .beads/dolt/lets && dolt push origin main` works fine (takes ~90 sec)
- `git ls-remote` confirms data was pushed despite bd reporting failure
- auto-push warnings appear on every bd command because of this

## Environment
- bd 0.56.1
- dolt 1.82.6
- Remote: git+https://github.com (private repo)
- macOS

## Suggested Fix

Use a longer timeout (or no timeout) for remote operations (push/pull). Regular queries are fast and benefit from 10s timeout, but remote ops need 2-5 minutes. Options:
1. Separate DSN for remote operations with longer timeouts
2. Remove readTimeout/writeTimeout from remote op connections
3. Make timeout configurable via config.yaml
title: bd dolt push/pull timeout: MySQL client readTimeout too short for git remote operations

description:
Sync bd create examples across codebase is part of a larger vision: extract reusable actions into skills that commands compose.

## Current problem
bd create examples in start.md, install.md, docs/knowledge/ don't include all required fields defined in rules. But the deeper issue is that commands contain inline logic for basic operations (take task, create branch, commit, etc.) instead of delegating to composable skills.

## Vision
Skills are always in context, so they trigger naturally in conversation even outside commands. Example: skill 'take task' - takes a task, creates branch, sets status. This skill is used by /lets:start command, but also fires when user just says 'take task lets-xyz' in regular conversation.

Commands = orchestrators that compose skills into workflows.
Skills = atomic reusable actions that work both inside commands and standalone.

## What to design
- Which actions should become skills (take task, create branch, commit, etc.)
- How skills compose inside commands
- How skill descriptions enable natural triggering
- Migration path from current inline logic to skill-based architecture

## Acceptance criteria
- Clear list of skills to extract
- Architecture design for skill composition
- At least one skill extracted as proof of concept
title: Design skill architecture - extract reusable actions from commands

description:
Root cause: Write tool requires manual absolute path construction. .lets easily becomes lets (missing dot). Bash commands use variables ($ROOT/.lets/) so they're safe, but Write tool calls are manual and error-prone.

Evidence: session-end wrote to lets/sessions/ instead of .lets/sessions/ despite skill template and CLAUDE.md being correct.

## Options to investigate
1. Add PreToolUse hook that validates Write paths containing 'lets/sessions' have the dot prefix
2. Change session-end skill to use bash for file writing instead of Write tool
3. Add .lets path as a constant in the skill that's resolved via bash first
4. Add lets/ (without dot) to .gitignore as safety net

In general we need to automate this - manual path construction for hidden dirs is a recurring problem, not just a one-off. Need a systematic solution (hook, lint, or convention) that catches this class of errors automatically.

This happened once but the pattern (manual path construction for hidden dirs) could repeat.
title: Prevent .lets path typos - dot prefix validation

description:
Currently /lets:start always runs full cycle: last-summary + git state + bd ready (full list) + task selection question. This is overhead when user already knows what to work on.

## Proposed modes

### 1. /lets:start <task-id> - quick start with specific task
- Skip bd ready and task selection
- Show only bd show <task-id> + comments (task context)
- Create/switch branch immediately
- Much faster for known work

### 2. /lets:start (no args) - full flow as today
- Last session summary
- Git state
- bd ready list
- Task selection question

### 3. /lets:start --continue - resume last in_progress task
- Find last in_progress task automatically
- Skip selection, go straight to branch
- Good for multi-session tasks

### 4. /lets:start --quick - minimal output
- Skip last-summary, skip full bd ready
- Just git state + task selection (compact)

## Open questions
- How to pass arguments to skills in Claude Code? Need to verify syntax
- Should full bd ready be lazy-loaded (only if user asks)?
- Can we detect if there's an obvious next task (only 1 in_progress) and auto-suggest?

## Acceptance criteria
- /lets:start with task ID skips selection and goes straight to branch
- /lets:start without args works as before (backwards compatible)
- At least one quick mode implemented
- Context recovery (bd show + comments) works in quick mode
title: Optimize /lets:start with quick modes and task argument

description:

## What to add to session summary
- Lifehacks discovered during session (shortcuts, tricks, patterns that worked)
- Nuances and gotchas encountered (things that surprised or confused)
- Open questions - things we didn't resolve, need to think about
- Ideas that came up but weren't tracked (informal thoughts)
- Blocked moments - what blocked us and how we unblocked
- Context that would be lost after compaction (why we made certain choices)
- Connections noticed between tasks/areas
- What worked well in this session (process improvements)

## Current state
Check commands/end.md to see what's saved now and redesign the summary template.

## Key principle
Summary is for CONTEXT RECOVERY - next session's Claude should feel like it was here. Not a dry log, but useful institutional memory.

## Acceptance criteria
- Richer summary template in /lets:end
- Captures lifehacks, nuances, open questions
- Easy to scan at session start
- Backwards compatible (old summaries still work)
title: Refactor session summary content in /lets:end

description:
PR workflow creates multiple files in .lets/ folder. Question: which of these are actually needed as files, and which can be fetched live from GitHub via gh CLI?

## Current state
Check what files PR workflow creates in .lets/ and evaluate each:
- Can this be fetched from GitHub on demand? (gh pr view, gh api, etc.)
- Does it change frequently? (then don't cache - always fetch fresh)
- Is it needed offline? (probably not)
- Is it used by other commands? (check cross-references)

## Goal
Minimize file storage. If GitHub is the source of truth - read from GitHub, don't duplicate locally. Files should only exist when:
1. Data doesn't exist on GitHub (local-only context)
2. Data is expensive to compute (not just an API call)
3. Data is needed after PR is closed/deleted

## Acceptance criteria
- Audit all .lets/ files created by PR workflow
- Remove files that can be replaced by gh CLI calls
- Keep only files with genuine local-only value
- PR workflow still works with fewer files
title: Reduce file storage in PR workflow - fetch from GitHub instead
